name: Python
summary: A programming language for calculations, automation, data analysis and prototypes.
why: This is the most reusable programming starting point across your robotics, spacecraft and thermal interests. Learn to explain and debug small programs before relying on large generated projects.
firstProject: Write a unit-conversion and component-mass calculator. Check five inputs independently, then plot a recorded sensor signal.
platform: Windows, macOS and Linux; check the current release.

name: Visual Studio Code
summary: An editor in which you write, run and debug code.
why: Use one editor consistently for Python, C/C++, documentation and Git. The editor organizes your work; the language runtime and compiler are separate components.
firstProject: Open a project folder, run a Python file, set a breakpoint and inspect a variable.
access: Free Microsoft distribution; extension and AI service terms vary.
platform: Windows, macOS and Linux; check the current release.

name: Git
summary: Version control that records changes to files and lets teams work on branches.
why: Keep calculations, code, assumptions and test revisions together. This is a small continuous habit, not a subject requiring equal time with mechanics or programming.
firstProject: Commit a working calculator, make an experimental branch and restore a prior result.
platform: Windows, macOS and Linux; check the current release.

name: GitHub
summary: A hosting and collaboration platform for Git repositories.
why: Use repositories, issues and pull requests to make engineering work reproducible and reviewable. Keep large binary CAD and test datasets in a storage workflow appropriate to their size.
firstProject: Publish a small project with a README, input data, run instructions and one issue describing the next experiment.
access: Free and paid plans; storage, automation and organizational limits vary.
platform: Web; desktop and command-line clients available.

name: Linux / Ubuntu + WSL
summary: A computing environment used to run development tools and many robotics systems.
why: Start with folders, processes, packages, permissions and the terminal. On Windows, WSL provides a useful practice environment; a robot or simulator may later need native Linux and specific device support.
firstProject: Run your Python calculator in Ubuntu, make an isolated environment and use Git from the terminal.
access: Ubuntu is free; WSL requires a supported Windows installation.
platform: Linux hardware or Ubuntu in WSL on supported Windows.

name: NumPy
summary: Fast arrays and mathematical operations for Python.
why: Learn array shapes, indexing and units. Vectors, matrices, sensor samples and state histories become easier to express consistently.
firstProject: Calculate the mass of a family of brackets from arrays of dimensions and material densities.
platform: Windows, macOS and Linux; check the current release.

name: Matplotlib
summary: A Python library for creating scientific plots.
why: Use labeled axes, units, uncertainty and clear comparisons. A figure should expose model error and trends, not just decorate a report.
firstProject: Plot measured and predicted temperature on one set of axes, with units and a legend.
platform: Windows, macOS and Linux; check the current release.

name: JupyterLab / Notebook
summary: An interactive workspace combining code, equations, results and explanatory text.
why: Useful for learning and investigating data. Restart and run all cells before sharing so the document reproduces its results from a clean state.
firstProject: Create a notebook explaining one calculation, its assumptions and a plot, then reproduce it from the top.
platform: Browser interface with a local or hosted Python environment.

name: SciPy
summary: Scientific Python algorithms for integration, optimization, interpolation and other numerical methods.
why: It becomes much more useful as you learn calculus, differential equations and numerical error. Understand the problem and solver assumptions before trusting a numerical answer.
firstProject: Integrate a simple cooling model and compare it with its known analytical solution.
platform: Windows, macOS and Linux; check the current release.

name: pandas
summary: A Python library for cleaning and analyzing tables of measurements.
why: Useful for timestamps, missing samples and repeated experiments. Preserve the original measurements and make each cleaning step explicit.
firstProject: Read a CSV test log, identify missing readings and compare average temperature across repeated trials.
platform: Windows, macOS and Linux; check the current release.

name: SymPy
summary: Symbolic mathematics inside Python, including algebra and calculus.
why: Use it to inspect derivations and compare symbolic and numerical solutions. It helps with equations, but does not establish whether your physical assumptions are appropriate.
firstProject: Differentiate a simple displacement function and check its velocity at several times.
platform: Windows, macOS and Linux; check the current release.

name: C++
summary: A compiled programming language used in robotics, simulation and performance-sensitive systems.
why: After Python, learn types, functions, memory ownership, compilation and debugging through small hardware or simulation tasks. Language competence is more valuable than collecting frameworks.
firstProject: Implement a sensor-reading buffer and test how it handles missing or invalid samples.
access: Language is not a paid product; free compilers are available.
platform: Windows, macOS and Linux; check the current release.

name: C
summary: A compiled language used close to embedded hardware and operating systems.
why: Learn pointers, arrays, memory and device interfaces. UCSD’s current MAE 144 description explicitly includes C and embedded Linux, while your future course’s actual tools should be checked near enrollment.
firstProject: Write and test a small state machine for a simulated fan and temperature sensor.
access: Language is not a paid product; free compilers are available.
platform: Windows, macOS and Linux; check the current release.

name: CMake
summary: A tool for configuring how compiled software projects are built.
why: It helps a C/C++ project locate libraries and build on different computers. Learn it when your code has several files or dependencies.
firstProject: Build a two-file C++ sensor utility and run its tests from a fresh build directory.
platform: Windows, macOS and Linux; check the current release.

name: GDB
summary: A debugger for inspecting running compiled programs.
why: Breakpoints and variable inspection make software behavior observable. This is especially valuable when C/C++ programs fail in ways that print statements do not explain.
firstProject: Find a deliberate out-of-range index in a small local C++ exercise using a breakpoint.
platform: GNU/Linux and supported toolchains; platform integration varies.

name: pytest
summary: A Python testing framework for checking program behavior automatically.
why: Engineering scripts deserve checks for units, known cases and invalid inputs. Learn this early enough that each new calculation comes with evidence it behaves as expected.
firstProject: Test a unit conversion with known values and ensure impossible inputs are rejected.
platform: Windows, macOS and Linux; check the current release.

name: Docker
summary: A container workflow for packaging software and its dependencies.
why: Helpful for reproducing a lab environment or sharing software with a team. Hardware access and real-time behavior still require deliberate setup; containers do not solve every deployment problem.
firstProject: Package an existing analysis script so another computer can produce the same plot.
access: Engine and Desktop terms differ; paid Desktop subscriptions apply in some organizations.
platform: Windows, macOS and Linux; check the current release.

name: SQLite / SQL
summary: A small local database engine and the query language used to retrieve structured records.
why: Useful when experiment metadata outgrows scattered CSV files. Keep each run linked to its configuration, measurements and notes.
firstProject: Store twenty experiment runs and query which configuration had the lowest average error.
platform: Windows, macOS and Linux; check the current release.

name: Blender
summary: A 3D creation suite for rendering, animation and visual assets.
why: Useful for explaining mechanisms and building scenes for visualization. Keep dimensioned mechanical design and engineering validation in the appropriate CAD and analysis tools.
firstProject: Import a finished CAD model and make a short exploded-view animation explaining assembly.
platform: Windows, macOS and Linux; check the current release.

name: ParaView
summary: An application for examining large scientific and simulation datasets.
why: Inspect slices, contours and time histories from numerical work. It is a post-processing tool: the underlying solver and validation determine the meaning of the picture.
firstProject: Open a tutorial flow dataset and compare a contour plot with numerical values along a line.
platform: Windows, macOS and Linux; check the current release.

name: LaTeX / Overleaf
summary: A document-writing workflow for equations, references and technical reports.
why: LaTeX is the typesetting system; Overleaf is a hosted editor. Use either when a report needs consistent equations and cross-references, or follow your team’s document template.
firstProject: Write a two-page experiment report with one equation, one figure and referenced sources.
access: LaTeX is free; Overleaf has free and paid plans.
platform: Local TeX distributions or a browser-based editor.

name: Zotero
summary: A reference manager for collecting, annotating and citing research.
why: Keep papers and vendor documentation organized by the question they answer. Useful across every specialty, particularly when a design decision needs a traceable source.
firstProject: Build a five-source collection for a material choice and export a bibliography.
platform: Windows, macOS and Linux; check the current release.

name: Julia
summary: A programming language designed for scientific and numerical computing.
why: An interesting later comparison once you can already build and validate models in Python or MATLAB. Learn it if a research group or numerical project gives you a reason.
firstProject: Reproduce a known cooling-model result in Julia and compare the numerical error.
platform: Windows, macOS and Linux; check the current release.

name: GNU Octave
summary: A free numerical-computing environment with syntax similar to MATLAB.
why: Useful for trying matrix-based calculations without a MATLAB license. Compatibility is incomplete, especially for specialized toolboxes and Simulink-dependent coursework.
firstProject: Solve a small linear system and plot the residual error.
platform: Windows, macOS and Linux; check the current release.
